title: Water system IQ, OQ and PQ to EU GMP Annex 15 | Aquemi
meta: IQ and OQ to protocols your QA approves, then PQ in three phases over 12 months (WHO TRS 1033, FDA guide), with alert levels set from your own data.
eyebrow: IQ · OQ · PQ · EU GMP ANNEX 15 · WHO TRS 1033
headline: IQ, OQ and a year of PQ your inspector can follow
lead: We commission your water or pure steam system, execute installation and operational qualification (IQ/OQ) to protocols your quality unit approves, and run performance qualification (PQ) with you until you hold 12 months of data.
primary_cta_intent: Review of a document you have|C&Q plan or validation master plan (VMP)

secondary_cta.label: How FAT feeds IQ and OQ

blocks.intro: Inspectors fault the evidence, not the water. Commissioning is documented but does not replace qualification (WHO TRS 1033, 11.2). We plan every stage in one commissioning and qualification (C&Q) plan your quality unit approves.

items.d: Flushing, pressure test, passivation, loop checks, start-up, punch list. Leverageable where documented to good documentation practice.
Wet test at our shop, repeated on your utilities; protocols approved before execution (Annex 15, 2.6).
The installed system matches the approved design: drawings, materials, welds, finish, slopes, dead legs, instruments (Annex 15, 3.9).
Performs across its operating ranges, worst case included (Annex 15, 3.11). After OQ you finalize procedures and training.
Required quality, reproducibly, across the seasons: three phases, at least 12 months.
Data and changes reviewed, for example annually (WHO TRS 1033, 14.1). Requalify only what they point to.

blocks.caption: ALERT AND ACTION LEVELS
blocks.h: Alert levels come from your data
blocks.intro: Pharmacopoeial limits are the specification, not an early warning. Annex 1, 6.13 expects alert levels based on qualification data.

rows.v: ≤ 1.3 µS/cm @ 25 °C (USP <645> stage 1); TOC ≤ 0.50 mg/L (USP <643>); < 0.25 EU/mL for WFI (USP <85>)
rows.m: Water fails; batch impact assessed

rows.v: ≤ 100 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL for Purified Water (PW), ≤ 10 CFU/100 mL for WFI, lower where justified
rows.m: Root-cause investigation; WFI organisms identified · USP <1231>; WHO TRS 1033, 12.9

rows.v: Provisional from phases 1 and 2, confirmed on the full year
rows.m: Trended as early warning · Annex 1, 6.13; WHO TRS 1033, 12.7

rows.v: A rule your quality unit agrees, such as a run of rising results
rows.m: Sanitization or maintenance adjusted under change control

blocks.h: Questions validation and quality teams ask

items.q: Do we really have to wait a year before using the water?
items.a: No. WHO TRS 1033 allows use during phase 2 when phase 1 and ongoing phase 2 data show the required quality and your QA approves it, and water is in use throughout phase 3. The year completes validation across the seasonal changes in your feed water. Plan first batches against the end of phase 2.

items.q: Can IQ and OQ be combined into one protocol?
items.a: Yes. Annex 15, 2.5 and 3.10 allow a combined installation and operational qualification (IOQ) where the system's complexity allows. On a packaged PW skid it often saves a review cycle; on a full generation, storage and pure steam system we usually keep them apart so IQ deviations do not hold up OQ testing of unaffected parts.

items.q: How much of IQ and OQ can FAT replace?
items.a: Documentation review and tests whose result transport and installation cannot change, where your quality unit accepts it (Annex 15, 3.6). We mark candidate tests in the C&Q plan and write the FAT protocol for your approval before execution. Water quality on your feed, site utilities and field-built piping are always proven on site. See FAT and SAT.

items.q: We work to ASTM E2500 verification, not IQ/OQ/PQ. Can you work that way?
items.a: Yes. The tests are much the same; the structure changes. Under ASTM E2500 and the ISPE Baseline Guide Vol. 5, verification focuses on critical aspects found by risk assessment, subject matter experts carry more of the review, and your quality unit approves acceptance and release. We write the C&Q plan in your model.

items.q: Who takes the PQ samples and who tests them?
items.a: Usually your operators and laboratory, because the routine monitoring that follows is theirs, and the method must stay the same from phase 1 onward. We write or review the sampling plan and train your samplers. Sampling by our staff in phases 1 and 2: [on-site PQ sampling by Aquemi, yes or no].

items.q: What happens if an action level is exceeded during PQ?
items.a: It is a deviation under your procedure. We investigate with you: sampling technique, sample valve, flush and use pattern, sanitization records, neighbouring points. The fix is verified by resampling; if it changes a procedure or setpoint, the phase may be extended. An excursion found, explained and corrected is stronger evidence than none.

Annex 15, 4.1 and 4.2 ask for evaluation at a justified frequency, not a full repeat. Most sites review the system annually, as WHO TRS 1033, 14.1 suggests, and requalify only what a change, a trend or the review points to. Repeating a full IQ/OQ every year by habit costs downtime and proves little.

items.q: Can you qualify or requalify a system you did not build?
items.a: Yes. We start with a gap assessment of the existing qualification file and the installed system against Annex 15, Annex 1 and your current requirements, then propose a scope your quality unit can approve. Missing as-built drawings, a dead leg register or calibration history are the usual gaps. See upgrades and requalification.
